keep-running.description: Keep the application running when its last window closes.

start-workspace.description:
The workspace opened at start: a workspace's name, or `"last"` for the one
that was open when the application closed.

x-lume-settings.help: The workspace Lume opens with
x-lume-settings.label: On launch

appearance.description: How things look: the theme and what overrides it.

accent.description:
The colour focus, the selected tab, selected text and the window's glow are
drawn in: `mint`, `blue`, `lilac`, `amber`, `coral` or `graphite`, each of which
suits both dark and light themes, or a colour of your own written `#rrggbb`.
Left out, the theme's.

x-lume-settings.help: Focus, selection, the tab highlight and the window's glow
x-lume-settings.label: Accent colour

background-blur.description: How much the picture is blurred, in pixels. Left out, the theme's.

background-image.description: A picture shown behind the panes: the path of an image file.

x-lume-settings.help: The path of an image file shown behind the panes
x-lume-settings.label: Picture

background-opacity.description: How opaque the picture is, from 0 to 1. Left out, the theme's.

card-radius.description:
The radius of a pane's corners, in pixels. Menus and palettes follow it. Left
out, the theme's.

x-lume-settings.help: The radius of a pane's corners, and of menus and palettes
x-lume-settings.label: Pane corners

control-radius.description:
The radius of the corners of tabs, buttons, fields and menu items, in pixels.
Nothing smaller inside them is rounder. Left out, the theme's.

x-lume-settings.help: The radius of tabs, buttons, fields and menu items
x-lume-settings.label: Control corners

dim-unfocused.description:
How much a pane without the focus is dimmed, from 0 (not at all) to 1. Left
out, the theme's.

x-lume-settings.help: How much a pane without the keyboard is dimmed
x-lume-settings.label: Dim unfocused panes

gap.description: The space between panes and around them, in pixels. Left out, the theme's.

motion.description:
Effects plugins bring for places in the window, each as `<plugin>/<effect>`.
A place left out moves as Lume's own does.

panel-enter.description: How a docked panel comes in.

pill-enter.description: How the pill of a pane put away appears.

status-change.description: How a status item shows that it changed.

pane-header.description: When a pane shows its header.

oneOf.description: Only in a tab with more than one pane.

x-lume-settings.help: Auto hides it in a tab with a single pane
x-lume-settings.label: Pane header

additionalProperties.description:
A tile for the program a pane runs: a kind of program, drawn with a line drawing
on a colour of the terminal's palette, or a well-known program, drawn with its mark
on its colour. A shell shows the prompt unless one of the shells' marks is chosen
for it.

oneOf.description: A prompt: a shell, or a program nothing else fits.
A page being written: an editor or a pager.
Git's mark: Git and the tools that work on it.
A pulse: a monitor of the system or of a process.
A globe: a connection to another machine.
A box: containers and virtual machines.

program-icons.description:
The tile a pane's header and its tab show for a program, by the program's name
without its folder or `.exe`, such as `nvim = "editor"`. These come before the
tiles the application knows.

anyOf.description:
How the mark on the tab on show moves to another tab. Each moves at once when the
keyboard changes the tab, and when the system asks for less motion.

oneOf.description:
A lit pill in the tab's colour that stretches towards the tab and settles,
glowing more the faster it goes.
A line under the tab that stretches towards the next one.
A plain pill that springs into place.
No motion: the mark is simply on the other tab.

anyOf.description: Something a plugin brings, as <plugin>/<name>

tab-highlight.description: How the mark on the tab on show moves to another tab.

x-lume-settings.help: How the highlight moves when another tab is shown
x-lume-settings.label: Tab highlight

theme.description:
The theme to use whatever the system's colour scheme is. Left out, the theme
follows the system: `theme-light` or `theme-dark`.

x-lume-settings.help: Colours for every window, terminal and pane
x-lume-settings.label: Theme

theme-dark.description: The theme used when the system's colour scheme is dark.

x-lume-settings.help: The theme used while the system is dark
x-lume-settings.label: In dark mode

theme-light.description: The theme used when the system's colour scheme is light.

x-lume-settings.help: The theme used while the system is light
x-lume-settings.label: In light mode

tile-color.description:
Which program tiles are drawn in their colours. The others are drawn in the
theme's muted ink.

oneOf.description: The tiles of the pane with the focus and of the tab it is in.
The tiles of the tab on show and of its panes.
None: every tile is drawn in the theme's muted ink.

x-lume-settings.help: Which tabs and pane headers show program icons in colour
x-lume-settings.label: Program icon colour

tokens.description:
Design tokens set over the theme's, written as a theme file writes them: a
table for each group, such as `[appearance.tokens.color]` with `accent = "#ff8800"`.

default-profile.description:
The profile new terminals use, by its id. Empty, new terminals run the shell of
`terminal.shell`.

x-lume-settings.help: Used for new terminal tabs and panes. A workspace's own choice comes first
x-lume-settings.label: Default terminal

fallback.description:
The fonts tried, in order, for a character the first has no glyph for, or when
it is not installed.

family.description: The font terminals are drawn in.

line-height.description: The height of a line of terminal text, as a multiple of the font's size.

x-lume-settings.help: The height of a line of terminal text, as a multiple of its size
x-lume-settings.label: Line height

size.description: The size of terminal text, in pixels.

ui-family.description: The font of everything that is not a terminal: tabs, headers, menus.

ui-size.description: The size of that text, in pixels.

weight.description: The weight of ordinary text, as fonts number weights: 400 is regular.

host.description: The session host, which runs the programs in the terminals.

idle-exit.description:
How long, in seconds, the session host stays with no window and no running
program before it exits, when programs are kept running after the application
closes. Zero keeps it running.

x-lume-settings.help: With no window open and no program running. 0 keeps it running
x-lume-settings.label: Session host exits when idle after

mode.description: Where the session host runs. Read when the application starts.

oneOf.description:
In a process of its own, which keeps the programs running when the application
closes, crashes or is updated; the application shows them again when it starts.
Inside the application: the programs end when it closes.

x-lume-settings.help: After Lume closes, programs keep running and come back when it starts again. Takes effect the next time Lume starts
x-lume-settings.label: Keep programs running

anyOf.description: A command's id, or `"unbound"`.
A command with a context or arguments.

command.description: The id of the command the key runs.

when.description:
Where the key does so: context names joined by `&&`, each of which may be
negated with `!`. Left out, everywhere.

anyOf.description: Several, for a key that does different things in different contexts.

items.description: One binding of a key, written out.

command.description: The id of the command the key runs.

when.description:
Where the key does so: context names joined by `&&`, each of which may be
negated with `!`. Left out, everywhere.

additionalProperties.description: What a key is bound to.

keybindings.description:
Keys and the commands they run. A key is a chord such as `"ctrl+shift+t"`, or a
sequence of chords separated by spaces; its value is a command's id, a table
with `command`, `when` and `args`, or `"unbound"` to take a default away.

anyOf.description: A command's id, or `"unbound"`.
A command with a context or arguments.

command.description: The id of the command the key runs.

when.description:
Where the key does so: context names joined by `&&`, each of which may be
negated with `!`. Left out, everywhere.

Where the key does so: context names joined by `&&`, each of which may be

windows.description: Bindings that hold on Windows only.

layout.description: Where things are placed in a window.

new-pane-cwd.description: The directory a new pane's program starts in.

oneOf.description:
The directory of the pane the new one is opened from, where its shell says
which that is; otherwise as `workspace`.
The workspace's folder, or the home directory if it has none.

tab-placement.description: Where the list of tabs is.

oneOf.description: In the bar at the top of the window.
In a panel on the left.
In a panel on the right.

x-lume-settings.help: In the bar at the top, or in a panel at a side
x-lume-settings.label: Tab list

plugins.description: Settings of plugins, by plugin id.

profile.description:
Ways to start a terminal. Each is a `[[profile]]` table with an `id`; one with
the id of a profile the application made changes that profile.

items.description: One `[[profile]]` table: what it sets, and nothing for what it leaves out.

client.description: `ssh`: the client program, instead of the one found on this machine.

anyOf.description: What happens to a pane when its program ends.

oneOf.description: The pane closes if the program ended without an error, and stays otherwise.
The pane closes however the program ended.
The pane stays, and says how the program ended.

close-on-exit.description:
What happens to the pane when the program ends, instead of
`terminal.close-on-exit`.

cwd.description: The directory the terminal starts in.

env.description: Environment variables set for the program.

extra-args.description: `ssh`: arguments given to the client before the host.

font-size.description: The text size of this profile's terminals, in pixels.

hidden.description: Leave the profile out of lists. It can still be named.

host.description:
`ssh`: the machine, as it would be given to `ssh`: a name from the user's
OpenSSH configuration, a host name or an address.

icon.description: The name of the icon shown for it.

id.description:
The profile's id: what `default-profile`, commands and other entries name it by.
An id the application uses for a profile it made (`auto.pwsh`,
`auto.wsl.<distribution>`, `auto.ssh.<host>`) changes that profile.

anyOf.description: What a profile's terminal runs.

oneOf.description: The shell of a Linux distribution on this Windows machine.
A shell on another machine, through the OpenSSH client.

launcher.description: What the terminal runs. Needed unless the id is that of a generated profile.

login.description: `shell`: start the program as a login shell.

name.description: What the profile is called in lists.

program.description: `shell`: the program to run. Left out, the user's own shell.

anyOf.description: Whether a shell is told to report its directory and its commands.

oneOf.description: The shell is set up to report them, without its own files being changed.
The shell is started as it is.

shell-integration.description: Whether the shell is set up to report its directory and commands.

theme.description: The theme of this profile's terminals, instead of the window's.

user.description: `wsl` and `ssh`: the user to be there.

tier.description:
What terminals are drawn with. Anything but `auto` is for finding out why
drawing goes wrong on a machine.

connection-sharing.description:
Let terminals to one machine share a connection, so that only the first has to
sign in. It applies to the hosts listed from the OpenSSH configuration, and
only where the OpenSSH client can do it, which the one that comes with Windows
cannot.

control-persist.description:
How long a shared connection is kept after its last terminal closes, as
OpenSSH's `ControlPersist` takes it: `10m`, `yes`, `no`.

close-on-exit.description: What happens to a pane when its program ends.

oneOf.description: The pane closes if the program ended without an error, and stays otherwise.
The pane closes however the program ended.
The pane stays, and says how the program ended.

options.label: Close the pane if it succeeded

confirm-close.description: Whether closing a pane asks first.

x-lume-settings.help: Ask before closing a pane whose program is still running
x-lume-settings.label: Confirm before closing a pane

cursor-blink.description: Whether the cursor blinks, until a program says otherwise.

cursor-effect-length.description:
How long the cursor's trail and pulse last, as a share of each effect's own
length: 1 is as designed, 2 twice as long.

x-lume-settings.help: How long the trail and the pulse last, against their own length
x-lume-settings.label: Effect length

anyOf.description: What the cursor gives off when it changes shape or lands in another pane.

oneOf.description: A disc that grows from the cursor and fades.
A ring that grows from the cursor and fades.
A box that grows from the cursor's shape and fades.
An outline that grows from the cursor's shape and fades.

anyOf.description: Something a plugin brings, as <plugin>/<name>

cursor-pulse.description:
What the cursor gives off when it changes shape or moves to another pane. Off
while the system asks for less motion.

x-lume-settings.help: Drawn when the cursor changes shape, or moves to another pane
x-lume-settings.label: Cursor pulse

cursor-style.description: The cursor's shape, until a program chooses another.

anyOf.description: What the cursor leaves behind when it jumps.

oneOf.description: Nothing: the cursor is simply in its new place.
The cursor smears towards its new place, its leading edge first.
A band from the old place shrinks into the new one.
A glowing comet flies to the new place, its tail following.

anyOf.description: Something a plugin brings, as <plugin>/<name>

cursor-trail.description:
What the cursor leaves behind when it jumps a distance, or moves to another
pane. Off while the system asks for less motion.

x-lume-settings.help: Drawn when the cursor jumps, or moves to another pane
x-lume-settings.label: Cursor trail

hidden-release.description:
Let a pane that is out of sight, in a tab not on show or a float put down, let go
of its window's copy of the screen, and get it back from the session host when it
is shown again. Off, every pane keeps its copy all the time.

x-lume-settings.help: Panes in hidden tabs let go of their copy of the screen and get it back from the session host when shown
x-lume-settings.label: Let go of hidden panes

hidden-release-seconds.description:
How long, in seconds, a pane stays out of sight before it lets go of its copy of
the screen.

x-lume-settings.help: How long a pane stays out of sight before it lets go of its screen
x-lume-settings.label: Let go of hidden panes after

history-paging.description:
Keep only the newest lines in each window and fetch older ones from the session
host when the terminal is scrolled back to them or searched. Off, every window
keeps all of a terminal's scrollback itself, which costs memory twice over.

x-lume-settings.help: Windows keep only the newest lines and fetch older ones as you scroll back or search
x-lume-settings.label: Fetch older lines when needed

history-release-seconds.description:
How long, in seconds, a window keeps the older lines it fetched once the terminal
is back at its newest output.

x-lume-settings.help: How long fetched lines stay once you are back at the newest output
x-lume-settings.label: Let go of older lines after

long-command-seconds.description: How long a command runs, in seconds, before its end is notified.

x-lume-settings.help: How long a command runs before its end is notified
x-lume-settings.label: Long command

notify-long-command.description:
Show a desktop notification when a command that ran for a while ends in a window
that is not in use. It needs the shell to report its commands.

x-lume-settings.help: A desktop notification when a command ends in a window you are not using
x-lume-settings.label: Notify when a long command ends

padding.description: The space between a pane's edge and its text, in pixels. Left out, the theme's.

x-lume-settings.help: The space between a pane's edge and its text
x-lume-settings.label: Padding

scrollback-lines.description: How many lines that have scrolled off the top are kept.

x-lume-settings.help: Older lines are dropped past this limit. New terminals use it
x-lume-settings.label: Scrollback

shell.description:
The program a new terminal runs when no profile says otherwise. Empty, it is the
user's own shell.

shell-args.description: The arguments that program is started with.

window-history-lines.description:
How many lines a window keeps for a terminal while older ones are fetched when
needed.

x-lume-settings.help: The newest lines a window holds itself when older ones are fetched as needed
x-lume-settings.label: Lines kept in the window

bell-attention.description:
Ask for attention when a program rings the bell in a window that is not in use:
the taskbar button flashes, or the dock icon bounces.

x-lume-settings.help: When a program rings the bell in a window you are not using
x-lume-settings.label: Flash the window on a bell

close-with-last-tab.description: Close a window when its last tab closes.

x-lume-settings.label: Close a window with its last tab

confirm-close.description: Whether closing a window with running programs asks first.

x-lume-settings.help: Ask before closing a window while programs are still running in it
x-lume-settings.label: Confirm before closing a window

corners.description:
How round the corners of a window's own frame are, where the window system lets
the application choose: Windows 11.

oneOf.description: As round as the window system makes them.

x-lume-settings.help: The corners of the window itself
x-lume-settings.label: Window corners

restore-bounds.description: Open windows where they were when the workspace was last open.

x-lume-settings.help: Open windows where they were when the workspace was last open
x-lume-settings.label: Restore window positions

anyOf.description: Who draws a window's title bar.

oneOf.description: The application draws it, as part of the top bar.

title-bar.description:
Who draws the title bar. Left out, the application draws it on Windows and
macOS, and the window system does on Linux.

x-lume-settings.help: Who draws the bar at the top of a window
x-lume-settings.label: Title bar

on-switch.description: What happens to a workspace's programs when another workspace is opened.

oneOf.description:
They keep running, and the workspace's panes show them again when it is opened
again.
